problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to service six critical substations across a regional power grid:

Substation Alpha: Grid coordinates (91,187)
Substation Beta: Coordinates (120,145)
Substation Gamma: Coordinates (43,178)
Substation Delta: Coordinates (172,52)
Substation Epsilon: Coordinates (196,14)
Substation Zeta: Coordinates (173,40)

The fiber-optic communication links between substations, which dictate travel pathways, have the following exact lengths in kilometers:
Alpha to Gamma: 48.8 km
Alpha to Delta: 157.4 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 202.4 km
Alpha to Zeta: 168.3 km
Beta to Gamma: 83.8 km
Beta to Delta: 106.6 km
Beta to Epsilon: 151.4 km
Beta to Zeta: 117.6 km
Gamma to Delta: 180.3 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 224.3 km
Gamma to Zeta: 189.6 km
Delta to Epsilon: 44.9 km
Delta to Zeta: 12.0 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 34.7 km

Due to incompatible network protocols, a direct connection between Substation Alpha and Substation Beta is prohibited. Furthermore, a critical network redundancy rule stipulates that exactly one of the following two backbone links must be actively traversed in the service circuit: the link between Substation Beta and Gamma, or the link between Substation Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient inspection circuit that visits each substation precisely once, concluding at the origin point, while minimizing the total distance traveled.
